clue.text: Novel missiles in black, gold (golden). -and the blue

definitions.text: Novel missiles in black, gold (golden). -and the blue

parts.words: Novel missiles in black, gold (golden). -and the blue
parts.note: the missiles that appear in several novel titles: Stevenson's The Black Arrow, Conrad's The Arrow of Gold, Mary Webb's The Golden Arrow

explanation.surface: A list of colours in which missiles from fiction are found.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed punctuation is scrambled by the scan, but the sense is clear: weapons named in titles such as The Black Arrow and The Arrow of Gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Shafts shot from a bow are the missiles named in each of these book titles.

clue.text: A goal from Davies

parts.note: a goal or aspiration, and also the title of a poem by the Welsh poet W. H. Davies

explanation.surface: A footballer named Davies scores.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests football; the word is a general aim, and a title by the poet W. H. Davies.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal is something one strives for, so the word for a driving aspiration fits.

clue.text: "He who runs may read" (and he who sits still perhaps)

definitions.text: "He who runs may read" (and he who sits still perhaps)

parts.words: "He who runs may read" (and he who sits still perhaps)
parts.note: the proverb says a runner can read something plain at a glance; the seated person, with more leisure, may go over the text a second time

explanation.surface: A gloss on the proverb about plain writing that even a runner can read.
explanation.definitionFit: Going over a text again is what a leisurely seated reader does, in contrast to the hurried runner.

clue.text: Dog from London (4, )

parts.note: a canine creation of the American novelist Jack London, not a dog from the British capital

explanation.surface: A dog that comes from the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: London is the writer Jack London, not the city; the wolf-dog title character of his 1906 novel. The stray '(4, )' is scan debris.
explanation.definitionFit: The title animal of Jack London's novel is a wolf-dog, so it is a dog from that author.

clue.text: Girl joins second friend for composer

parts.note: a chum is a friend
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl teams up with another friend in honour of a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Schumann was a German Romantic composer of songs and piano music.

clue.text: Edgeworth's stretch over amount paid to support move to protect ruler

parts.note: in chess, castling is the move that tucks the king safely behind a rook
to rack is to stretch on the torture rack
rent is the amount paid for a lodging

explanation.surface: Someone stretches the budget to keep a ruler safe.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a down clue, so 'over' and 'to support' only set the order of the pieces from top to bottom; Edgeworth is the Anglo-Irish novelist Maria Edgeworth.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria Edgeworth's 1800 novel about an Irish estate bears this title, so it is her book.

clue.text: It's case is capital

parts.note: the kind of case whose letters are capitals, as typesetters call big letters

explanation.surface: A remark that something's case is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like praise or money; it means capital letters, which printers kept in the top case of type.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital letters are called by this case name because printers stored them in the higher tray.

clue.text: How to calm an actor, holding annual statistics

indicators.note: the words calm an actor hold the answer within them, running across the word gaps

explanation.surface: Advice on soothing an actor while keeping yearly figures.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearbook of facts and figures is published each year, so it holds annual statistics.

clue.text: Comfy home alternative for Greek elder statesman

parts.note: a nest is a cosy home
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A cosy house or something else, for an old Greek politician.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer, the aged king of Pylos is the wise senior counsellor of the Greeks at Troy.

clue.text: Useful small red letters used in downbeat verse

indicators.note: used, as in worn and knocked about, tells us these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Handy little red letters appearing in gloomy poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' is the anagram signal on USEFUL SMALL RED; 'letters' and 'in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Baudelaire's collection The Flowers of Evil is famously dark and melancholy poetry.

clue.text: Visually challenged naval writer?

definitions.meaning: the blind beggar healed by Jesus in Mark's Gospel bore this name
the pen name of Lewis Ricci, who wrote stories of Royal Navy life

explanation.surface: A sailor who wrote despite poor eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the Gospel's blind man and to a Royal Navy officer who wrote under it.

clue.text: Some cheap verse by Joyce

parts.note: Joyce's small poetry collection ... Penyeach, a title meaning poems costing a penny each

explanation.surface: A dismissive comment on Joyce's poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheap' is literal: the full title says the poems are a penny each.
explanation.definitionFit: Joyce called his 1927 booklet of thirteen poems by this playful spelling, priced as a penny apiece.

clue.text: Arnold Bennett's thief may get into hot water

definitions.meaning: rhyming slang for a thief, used in Bennett's fiction
a fragment of tea dropped into the pot gets into boiling water

explanation.surface: A thief from a Bennett story risks getting into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang the phrase rhymes with 'thief'; 'hot water' is both trouble and the teapot.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang pairs it with thief, and a bit of tea is steeped in boiling water.

clue.text: Jessica carried a torch for him

definitions.text: Jessica carried a torch for him

parts.words: Jessica carried a torch for him
parts.note: in The Merchant of Venice Shylock's daughter elopes with the man she loves, dressed as his torchbearer

explanation.surface: A woman named Jessica was in love with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carried a torch' is both being in love and, literally, Jessica acting as torchbearer when she runs away with her lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Jessica loves and elopes with this young Venetian.

clue.text: Nameless bard, or Italian

indicators.note: name-less means the letter N, for name, is removed

parts.note: Ossian is the legendary Gaelic bard of Macpherson's poems

explanation.surface: An anonymous poet, possibly from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: In Italian the word means 'or', and in music marks an alternative passage.

clue.text: Lyrist's friend staged by Mallet

definitions.meaning: the beloved wife of Orpheus, the mythic player of the lyre
the title of a 1731 tragedy by the Scottish dramatist David Mallet

explanation.surface: A musician's companion put on stage by a hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mallet' looks like a tool but is the playwright David Mallet.
explanation.definitionFit: She was Orpheus's wife in myth, and Mallet wrote a stage tragedy named after her.

clue.text: Unlike Clemo's' percussionist

definitions.meaning: Jack Clemo's autobiographical book is A ... Drummer, so his drummer is described by this word

explanation.surface: A drummer quite unlike anyone in Clemo's band.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Clemo was a Cornish poet; the stray apostrophe is scan debris.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not alike is of another sort, which is what this adjective means.

clue.text: He observed dramatic values

parts.note: the theatre critic C. E. ... wrote a book of reviews called Dramatic Values

explanation.surface: Someone who kept an eye on standards in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: C. E. Montague of the Manchester Guardian published his drama criticism under the title Dramatic Values.

clue.text: French shepherd with account of provenance of renowned duellist

parts.note: berger is the French word for shepherd

explanation.surface: A French shepherd tells the story of a famous swordsman's origins.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyrano, the celebrated swordsman of Rostand's play, takes his name from this town in France.

clue.text: Cutting passage

definitions.meaning: a cutting is an extract clipped from a publication
a passage is a section taken from a longer text

explanation.surface: A slicing corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a press clipping and a selected section of text are extracts from a longer work.

clue.text: Collins offered Foreign Office's firm count

parts.note: the possessive ending gives S
CO, company, is a firm

explanation.surface: Collins offered a government department a reliable figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilkie Collins created the villainous Count of this name in The Woman in White; 'Collins offered' points to him.
explanation.definitionFit: The scheming Italian nobleman of The Woman in White holds the title of count.

clue.text: Holiday spot visited by Shute?

parts.note: Nevil Shute's novel On the Beach places its characters at the shore, a typical holiday destination

explanation.surface: A resort where the novelist Shute went.
explanation.walkthrough: Shute's best-known novel is On the Beach, hence the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The coast is the classic holiday destination, and Shute's characters wait out their end on the beach.

clue.text: "They are the ruthless versicles of the Galsworthy age", said Grigson of his poems

definitions.text: "They are the ruthless versicles of the Galsworthy age", said Grigson of his poems

parts.words: "They are the ruthless versicles of the Galsworthy age", said Grigson of his poems
parts.note: the critic Geoffrey Grigson's sharp verdict on the verse of a poet of that era

explanation.surface: A critic's scathing quotation about another poet's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Grigson aimed this barb at Harry Graham, author of the comic Ruthless Rhymes.

clue.text: Stage king free of inner character

indicators.note: inner tells us the character goes inside the word for free

parts.note: to rid is to free
CHAR is short for character

explanation.surface: A theatre monarch freed from his true nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare put several English kings of this name on stage, notably the Second and Third.

clue.text: Borges's first letter is not really a help

indicators.note: not really, meaning not in its true form, says these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A claim that a writer's opening letter is unhelpful.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet and the title of a famous Borges story.

clue.text: Erect an alteration to stage again

indicators.note: an alteration changes the order of the letters in erect an

explanation.surface: Putting up an extension in order to perform once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To act out an event a second time is to perform or stage it again.

clue.text: Deighton's was submerged

parts.note: Len Deighton's thriller ... Under Water names an animal that went beneath the surface

explanation.surface: Something belonging to Deighton sank.
explanation.definitionFit: Deighton's 1963 novel title has this animal under water, that is, submerged.

clue.text: Motorway queen gets on the bypass for Scots guy, say

parts.note: Anne was a British queen
a ring road is a bypass, shortened to ring

explanation.surface: A queen joins the ring road off the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy Mannering is a novel by Walter Scott; 'say' marks Guy as one example of the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Scott's novel Guy Mannering gives its hero this surname, so the guy is Scott's.

clue.text: Streetcar passenger Harold

parts.note: a character in A Streetcar Named Desire, Harold, known as Mitch, Stanley's friend

explanation.surface: A man named Harold riding a tram.
explanation.walkthrough: Streetcar is Tennessee Williams's play A Streetcar Named Desire, not a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Blanche's suitor Mitch in A Streetcar Named Desire has the full name Harold with this surname.

clue.text: Some of Hardy's Egdon Heath energy suggests Odysseus's adviser

indicators.note: some of says part of the letters of the following words are used

explanation.surface: Part of Hardy's Egdon Heath energy hints at a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardy's Egdon Heath is the moorland in The Return of the Native.
explanation.definitionFit: The goddess of wisdom guides and advises Odysseus throughout the Odyssey.
